scenarios.name: delete-fails
scenarios.why: LGDPDB01's DELETE fails (SQLCODE -904): it sets CA-RETURN-CODE '90' and LINKs LGSTSQ, whose WRITEQ is refused (X6): the task is judged up to it, so LGDPOL01's If CA-RETURN-CODE > 0 (line 127) is not reached

notes: GenApp's delete-policy front end (LGDPOL01, LINKed with the 32500-byte LGCMAREA COMMAREA): it checks the COMMAREA and LINKs LGDPDB01 (which LINKs LGDPVS01) with it. The case runs every program of that chain in the same task ("programs"), LGSTSQ too (its error logger, "region" for its ASSIGN SYSID), with the back-end case's Db2 tables, VSAM file and data; the scenarios reuse genapp-lgdpdb01's inputs (each "why" names its source) and add the front end's own paths: no-commarea (EIBCALEN 0: LGSTSQ, ABEND LGCA). The request id is upper-cased first (request-lowercase); an unknown one is '99' with no LINK. If CA-RETURN-CODE > 0 after the LINK (line 127) is reached only through LGDPDB01's / LGDPVS01's error paths, which LINK LGSTSQ and are judged up to its refused WRITEQ (X6): delete-fails shows the path, the branch is not counted. WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE's IF EIBCALEN > 0 (and the IF EIBCALEN < 91 inside it) is never true: the paragraph is PERFORMed only when EIBCALEN is zero -- dead in practice, uncovered by every scenario. The SQL faults (M2) are the harness's, one per statement the tasks run.
